top_story.headline: A quiet weekend: no new registrations, ethics filings or unreported disclosures
top_story.dek: The only substantial activity was a batch of third-quarter lobbying reports, nine of them terminations.
paragraphs: The Office of Government Ethics logged 18 filings, all already covered in earlier editions. The Clerk of the House and Senate disclosure systems showed only filings reported previously, and the lobbying database held no new registrations.

sections.headline: No new OGE ethics filings to report
paragraphs: The Office of Government Ethics received 18 new filings during the reporting window, all of which have already been disclosed in prior editions of this newsletter.

sections.headline: No new lobbying registrations; 282 quarterly reports and amendments filed, nine of them terminations
paragraphs: The Senate lobbying database posted 282 filings from October 10 through the morning of October 11, 2026, and none were new registrations. Most were routine third-quarter activity reports (253 with activity, 17 reporting no activity). The issue areas named most often were Budget/Appropriations, Education and Transportation.
Nine filings terminate a lobbying relationship, listed below. Full filing list.

All House and Senate disclosure filings in the window (three House candidate reports and one Senate candidate report) were already reported in earlier editions, so that section is omitted.
